Subject: Post-call: VPC data flow & air-gapped option — recap and asks

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

• High-level ask: you want Redwood running inside a FinSecure VPC with no customer data leaving the VPC except for telemetry that you explicitly permit. You also asked about an air-gapped / on-prem variant for one of your regulated lines of business.
• Immediate clarification items we promised to follow up on: network egress controls (ports/IPs), where logs and telemetry are written (S3 vs. Cloud logging), PII residency/retention settings, and the feasibility of an air-gapped deployment for the compliance team.

Action items / owners:
1) I will circulate a first-pass dataflow diagram and list of outbound endpoints we need to whitelist (by Friday). (rafael_mendes)
2) Karthik to confirm technical constraints for air-gapped installs and outline minimal infra requirements. (karthik_iyer)
3) Monica to draft suggested retention defaults and logging controls we can include in the SOW. (monica_patel)

Can you confirm the compliance stakeholders we should include on the next call and any internal network reviewers? Also confirm whether the restricted workload will be in the us-east-1 AWS account or a different account/region.

I'll attach the diagram once Karthik sends the kernel-level notes.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes

Rafael, thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Telemetry: security team will allow only aggregated telemetry on port 443 to a fixed egress IP range. No raw request/response payloads may leave the VPC.
2) Logs: we prefer logs routed to our centralized S3 bucket (arn:aws:s3:::finsecure-audit-logs) with server-side encryption and restricted KMS key. Retention policy is 7 years for audit logs.
3) Air-gapped: compliance expects evidence of an air-gapped option — ideally an on-prem bundle we can run in an isolated VLAN. Can you confirm whether that option requires any external time-sync or licensing phone-home?

I’ll loop in our network reviewer (security@finsecure.com) for the whitelist.

-Alex

Rafael / Alex — thanks, I captured the minimal technical constraints. High level notes: 

• Hosted-in-VPC option (preferred): Redwood components run as customer-managed services inside your VPC. Outbound egress is limited to: 
  - telemetry.redwoodinference.com (443) -> allow by CIDR range 54.210.0.0/16
  - model-updates.redwoodinference.com (443) -> optional, can be disabled for frozen mode
  - kms.redwoodinference.com (443) -> only for customers who want managed keywrap; otherwise you can bring-your-own KMS and we do not call out.

• PII paths: request payloads and KV cache remain in your VPC. If you enable Redwood-managed caching to improve latency we will store cache entries on EBS volumes in your account; data residency remains inside the VPC. Any telemetry events are aggregated (no full payloads) and can be routed only to endpoints you whitelist.

• Air-gapped / on-prem: we support an on-prem bundle that does not require outbound phone-home for normal inference. Requirements: 
  - NTP/time sync to an internal time source (no external NTP required)
  - License key validated offline via a pre-generated signed token OR via an on-prem licensing appliance (your choice)
  - No external model downloads required if you ship a model bundle with the install (we can provide a signed model artifact).

Attached: redwood_vpc_dataflow_diagram.png (annotated flow showing which flows cross customer boundary) and short infra matrix in the footer.

If this looks good I’ll flatten the diagram into a one-page whitelist list for your network team.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: technical details — retention & logging defaults + SOW draft link

Alex / team — following up on retention and logging details. Below are the defaults we recommend and that we can include in the SOW; all are configurable to your requirements: 

Retention defaults (can be overridden in account config):
• Audit logs: 7 years (delivered to your S3 ARN; server-side encrypted with customer KMS)
• Access logs (service-level): 365 days
• Application debug traces: 30 days (configurable; we do not store request bodies in debug traces by default)

Logging controls and PII handling:
• By default Redwood redacts PII in telemetry and traces. Redaction rules are pluggable and we will work with your compliance team to tune them.
• Raw request/response payloads are never sent out of the VPC in the hosted-in-VPC option unless you explicitly opt into managed caching that stores cache entries on EBS in your account. Even then the data remains in your AWS account and is subject to your KMS controls.

Air-gapped specifics:
• Offline install requires an initial signed model artifact and a pre-generated signed license token. License token TTL is configurable; we recommend a 1-year TTL with renewal via an offline signed package. No periodic outbound phone-home is required for inference execution.

I’ve dropped a first-pass SOW and a one-page whitelist export link here: https://drive.google.com/finsecure-arch-draft (redwood_private_deploy_options.pdf inside).

Next steps: Rafael to coordinate a short session with your security and network reviewers to walk the diagram and the whitelist. Can we schedule 30 minutes the week of Sep 22?

Thanks,
